title: Unidentified tool outputs can be paired with unrelated identified calls during replay
reasoning: When a replayed tool-output has no resolvable correlation id, findMatchingPendingToolCallIndex falls back to returning the first pending call even if every pending call has its own correlation id. That can preserve a tool call/output pair that were never correlated, corrupting replay context with the wrong tool result. The inverse fallback for an identified output to an idless pending call may be a legacy compatibility path, but matching an idless output to an identified call has no evidence of a safe contract in the included code.
recommendation: Only use the positional fallback when both sides are idless, or when a documented legacy replay mode explicitly permits positional matching. If pending calls have correlation ids and the output does not, leave the output unmatched.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were included for replay filtering or mismatched correlation-id behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a test where messages contain two correlated tool-call entries followed by an idless tool-output, and assert buildReplayContextMessages drops the idless output instead of preserving it with the first call.
minimumFixScope: Update findMatchingPendingToolCallIndex matching rules and add focused replay-correlation tests.
